title: Propagate the merit-over-cost rule to subagent-planner (both copies)
description:
CAM-379 propagated the operator's merit-over-cost recommendation rule to the three cam agents that BUILD, GATE, and APPROVE (subagent-implementer, subagent-reviewer, subagent-auditor) in both .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/. The subagent-planner was left out and genuinely lacks the rule in both copies (verified: exhaustive grep for merit/over-cost/operational-cost/context-window/effort/undersize/oversize/scope-limiter returns only the frontmatter 'effort: xhigh'; the planner body never mentions cost, effort, 'v1', or 'future enhancement'). This is the last hole in the think->build->gate->approve governance chain: the planner AUTHORS the PRD scope and story decomposition, so it is precisely the agent that could undersize, oversize, or weaken a story's design approach for effort or cost reasons.

Scope: add a 'Merit over cost.' rule to the planner's '## Story Sizing Rules' section in BOTH .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md and templates/agents/subagent-planner.md, with planner-role framing (do not undersize/oversize/weaken a story's approach for cost reasons; rank by engineering merit; if a robust approach is expensive, note the cost separately after the recommendation without changing what is planned). The two must-survive clauses from CAM-379 must appear verbatim: (A) 'This rule limits the quality of the recommendation, not its scope: Simplicity remains the scope limiter.' and (B) 'Operational cost is never a criterion, but quality degradation from context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion, not a cost one.'

The two planner copies are currently byte-identical (205 lines, no deliberate divergence), so the inserted prose must be identical text in both. Because templates/agents/ is embedded into the compiled binary via scripts/generate-embedded-vendor.ts (src/vendor/_generated.ts), editing the templates copy requires an embed-vendor regen, and the change ships to adopters via a future cam init, so a coherence rebuild is required after merge.

Out of scope: do NOT change the implementer/reviewer/auditor/orchestrator copies (already done in CAM-379); do NOT reword the two must-survive clauses; do NOT reconcile the two planner copies into a shared file.
